parsed.study_design: Three-basin qualitative case study using document review, interviews, participant observation, and authors’ field experience
parsed.population_and_sample: Water users’ associations and water-governance institutions in the Pangani, Wami/Ruvu, and Lake Victoria/Mara basins; the paper describes at least 12, 16, and 6 WUAs in these respective case-study areas
parsed.exposure: Implementation of Tanzania’s National Water Policy, Water Resources Management Act, and legally recognized water users’ associations as participatory water-resource governance institutions
parsed.outcome: WUA formation, functionality, leadership, participation, financing, conflict resolution, fee collection, regulatory awareness, environmental management, and institutional sustainability; no household or community water/sanitation service-access outcome is assessed
parsed.rationale: The methods paragraph preceding “The Tanzanian Context for Freshwater Management” describes three basin case studies based on documents, interviews, participant observation, and the authors’ implementation experience. The “Water Users’ Associations: Progress and Challenges” and basin case-study sections report institutional performance and water-resource management activities, but do not evaluate household or community service connection, availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. It is therefore a water-resource governance study rather than an empirical study of household or community water or sanitation service access.
